summary: This section punishes anyone who uses the words "Limited" or "Private Limited" at the end of their business name without being properly registered as a company with limited liability. The punishment is a daily fine for every single day the improper name is used. It applies to any person or group carrying on business under such a title.
points: Forbids trading or carrying on business using "Limited" or "Private Limited" as the last words of a name without proper incorporation.
Applies to any person or group of persons using the unauthorized name or title.
Requires the business to be duly incorporated with limited liability to legally use these words.
Punishes offenders with a fine ranging from five hundred rupees up to two thousand rupees for every day the name is used.
example: Rahul and Amit decided to start a small stationery shop together. Without registering their business legally as a company, they printed a big signboard outside their shop that read "Rahul and Amit Stationery Private Limited". They wanted customers to trust them more by looking like a big registered company. However, because they did not complete the legal incorporation process to get limited liability, using "Private Limited" at the end of their business name is forbidden. As a result, Rahul and each of those persons are punishable with a daily fine for every single day that they used this unauthorized title for their shop.

terms.meaning: A word used at the end of a company name to show that the owners have limited liability.
Words used at the end of a private company name to show limited liability.
Legally formed and registered as a company.
A sum of money that must be paid as a punishment for breaking the law.

watch: People often confuse using these words casually with actually being legally registered as a company.
